def: A white mineral powder used topically as a mild astringent and skin protectant, as in diaper rash creams and sunscreens, where it physically blocks ultraviolet light.
A semisolid mixture of hydrocarbons refined from petroleum, used as an occlusive skin protectant and ointment base that traps moisture in skin.
Waiting 30 to 60 seconds or more after birth before clamping the umbilical cord, letting placental blood transfer to the newborn. Raises neonatal iron stores and hemoglobin and lowers anemia risk.
Excessive sweating beyond what is needed to regulate temperature. Can be primary (palms, soles, axillae) or secondary to infection, hyperthyroidism or drugs.
A handheld instrument with light and magnifier for examining the external ear canal and tympanic membrane.
Whitish vaginal discharge. A physiologic form increases with estrogen in pregnancy or ovulation; excessive or malodorous discharge suggests infection.
Inward turning of the eyelid margin so that lashes rub against the cornea, causing irritation and corneal damage. Often from aging or scarring.
Chronic inflammation of the eyelid margins causing red, crusted, itchy lids. Associated with staphylococcal infection and meibomian gland dysfunction.
The five long bones in the midfoot between tarsal bones and toes.
Congenital inward deviation of the forefoot with a normal hindfoot, giving a bean-shaped foot. Usually resolves spontaneously.
Congenital deformity of the foot and ankle, most commonly talipes equinovarus (clubfoot) with plantar flexion, inversion and forefoot adduction.
A defect or stress fracture of the pars interarticularis of a vertebra, often at L5 in young athletes. Causes low back pain and can lead to spondylolisthesis.
Sudden brief loss of consciousness from transient complete heart block or asystole causing a drop in cardiac output. Patient recovers quickly with a flushed look.
Excess body fat in children, defined as BMI at or above the 95th percentile for age and sex. Raises risk of type 2 diabetes, hypertension and fatty liver.
Infection occurring in a vaccinated person despite immunization, usually milder than in unvaccinated people.
Small cationic peptides of the innate immune system, such as defensins and cathelicidin, that kill microbes by disrupting their membranes.
Consumptive coagulopathy with thrombocytopenia caused by platelet trapping in a rapidly growing vascular tumor, such as kaposiform hemangioendothelioma, in infants.
Viruses that can cause cancer, such as HPV (cervical cancer), EBV (Burkitt lymphoma), HBV and HCV (hepatocellular carcinoma), HTLV-1 and HHV-8.
A secreted guidance protein that directs growing axons toward or away from its source through DCC and UNC5 receptors.
Autoimmune encephalitis with antibodies to NMDA receptors, mainly in young women, often with ovarian teratoma. Causes psychosis, seizures, dyskinesias and autonomic instability.
Immune-mediated inflammation of brain and spinal cord triggered by a distant cancer, often small cell lung cancer. Associated with anti-Hu antibodies.
A malignant glandular tumor with cystic spaces and papillary projections, as seen in the ovary.
A tumor of the pleura or peritoneum linked to asbestos exposure. Causes pleural effusion and chest pain; shows calretinin positivity.
Life-threatening reaction in spinal cord injury above T6, in which a noxious stimulus such as bladder distension causes severe hypertension, headache and bradycardia.
A monoclonal antibody against CTLA-4 that boosts T cell activity, used for melanoma. Causes immune-related colitis, hepatitis and endocrinopathies.
A germ cell tumor of the pineal or suprasellar region, histologically like testicular seminoma. Pineal tumors cause Parinaud syndrome; highly radiosensitive.
Transient apical ballooning of the left ventricle triggered by emotional or physical stress, mimicking myocardial infarction with normal coronary arteries. Thought to involve catecholamine surge.
Impaired voice production causing hoarseness or altered pitch and quality, due to laryngeal disease or vocal cord dysfunction.
Interventions that limit neuronal damage or death after insults such as ischemia or neurodegeneration.
The amount of ethanol in the blood, expressed as percent weight per volume. Legal driving limit in the US is 0.08%.
Mismatch between fetal head size and maternal pelvis preventing vaginal delivery, a cause of obstructed labor and cesarean section.
An RNA-guided endonuclease from CRISPR systems that cuts double-stranded DNA at a sequence matching a guide RNA, used for gene editing.
Weakness of the tracheal wall cartilage causing airway collapse during breathing, producing expiratory stridor or barking cough in infants.
Narrowing of the trachea, often after prolonged intubation or tracheostomy. Causes stridor and exertional dyspnea.
A constricting band placed on a limb to stop arterial bleeding or distend veins for venipuncture.
Ultrasound measurement of embryo length from top of head to buttocks in the first trimester. Most accurate method of dating pregnancy.
Complement activation triggered when C1 binds IgG or IgM antibody-antigen complexes, activating C4 and C2 to form C3 convertase. Deficiency of C1 to C4 predisposes to lupus.
Inflammation of the iris and ciliary body (anterior uveitis), causing painful red eye, photophobia and small irregular pupil. Associated with HLA-B27 diseases and sarcoidosis.
An antimuscarinic antispasmodic that relaxes gut smooth muscle, used in irritable bowel syndrome. Causes dry mouth and urinary retention.
A long-acting nonselective beta blocker, used for hypertension, angina and variceal bleeding prophylaxis.
A statistical method modeling a continuous outcome as a linear function of one or more predictors.
Blockage of a coronary artery, typically by thrombus on a ruptured plaque, causing myocardial infarction.
Bleeding in the putamen, the most common site of hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage. Causes contralateral hemiparesis and sensory loss from internal capsule involvement.
Folds in the lining of veins that prevent backflow of blood. Incompetence causes varicose veins and chronic venous insufficiency.
The ability to distinguish internal thoughts and fantasies from external reality. Impaired in psychosis, but intact in neurosis.
The deep vein of the thigh that continues as the external iliac vein. It lies medial to the femoral artery in the femoral triangle.
Infections from indwelling catheters, such as central line bloodstream infections and urinary tract infections. Biofilm formation is key; Staphylococcus is common.
A gas used to sterilize heat-sensitive equipment. It alkylates DNA and proteins.
A plasma enzyme that hydrolyzes succinylcholine and mivacurium. Deficiency or atypical variants cause prolonged paralysis after succinylcholine.
The joint between the first (atlas) and second (axis) cervical vertebrae permitting head rotation. Instability occurs in Down syndrome and rheumatoid arthritis.
An ergot alkaloid acting on serotonin receptors that constricts blood vessels. Used for acute migraine; overuse causes ischemia.
The second division of the trigeminal nerve (V2), carrying sensation from the midface, passing through the foramen rotundum.
The greatest volume of air a person can breathe in a minute with maximal effort. Reflects respiratory muscle strength and airway resistance.
Temporary storage of a small amount of information for seconds to minutes, such as digit span (about seven items).
Sweat glands over most of the body that secrete watery sweat for thermoregulation, controlled by sympathetic cholinergic fibers.
Blockage of nasal airflow from mucosal swelling, deviated septum, polyps or tumor.
Surgical removal of mastoid air cells, used for chronic mastoiditis or cholesteatoma.
An abnormal or surgically made connection between an artery and a vein. Used for hemodialysis access; large ones can cause high-output heart failure.
Intestinal infection by Shigella, causing bloody diarrhea with fever and cramps. Spread by fecal-oral route and via low infectious dose.
Fertilization of an egg by sperm outside the body, with the embryo transferred into the uterus. Used for infertility.
Complication of fertility drugs with enlarged ovaries and fluid shift from leaky vessels, causing ascites, pleural effusion and hemoconcentration.
Antibodies against hepatitis C virus, the initial screening test. They indicate exposure, so HCV RNA is needed to confirm active infection.
Accumulation of hemosiderin, an iron storage pigment, in tissues without necessarily causing damage. Occurs after repeated transfusions or hemolysis.
Fibrosis and thickening of the palmar fascia that pulls the fingers, especially the ring and little fingers, into flexion. Associated with alcoholism, diabetes and male sex.
Herniation of the rectum into the posterior vaginal wall from weak pelvic support. Causes pelvic pressure and difficult defecation.
Implanted electrodes delivering electrical pulses to targets such as the subthalamic nucleus, used for Parkinson disease and essential tremor.
Blood accumulating in the vagina because of an imperforate hymen or transverse vaginal septum. Presents with primary amenorrhea and cyclic pelvic pain.
Accumulation of surfactant proteins in alveoli from defective GM-CSF signaling. Causes dyspnea and a crazy-paving CT pattern; treated with whole-lung lavage.
A mite that burrows into skin and causes scabies, with intense nocturnal itching and burrows between fingers. Treated with permethrin.
Drugs or agents that stop bleeding, such as tranexamic acid, vitamin K and thrombin.
The lone star tick, which transmits Ehrlichia and causes alpha-gal allergy to red meat.
Fracture of the orbital floor or medial wall from blunt trauma, with entrapment of the inferior rectus muscle. Causes diplopia on upgaze and infraorbital numbness.
Removal of the entire breast, pectoral muscles and axillary lymph nodes.
The lowest part of the pharynx, from the hyoid to the cricoid cartilage, leading to the esophagus.
Brain infection by HSV-1 with predilection for the temporal lobes. Causes fever, seizures and altered behavior; treated with IV acyclovir.
Autosomal recessive neuropathy (Riley-Day syndrome) in Ashkenazi Jews from IKBKAP mutation. Causes lack of tears, labile blood pressure and insensitivity to pain.
A tyrosine kinase inhibitor of ALK and ROS1, used for non-small cell lung cancers with ALK rearrangement.
A physician order that cardiopulmonary resuscitation not be attempted if the heart or breathing stops.
Continuous measurement of exhaled carbon dioxide, used to confirm endotracheal tube placement and monitor ventilation.
A sealed dressing that blocks air and fluid, used for open pneumothorax (sucking chest wound) and to retain moisture.
A venomous spider (Latrodectus) whose neurotoxin (alpha-latrotoxin) triggers massive acetylcholine release, causing severe muscle cramps and abdominal rigidity.
Surgical removal of the vertebral lamina to decompress the spinal canal, used for spinal stenosis.
Bacterial overgrowth in a stagnant segment of small bowel after surgery, causing malabsorption, steatorrhea and vitamin B12 deficiency.
Abnormal connection allowing pancreatic juice to leak, often after surgery or pancreatitis.
Blood testing of neonates for treatable congenital disorders such as phenylketonuria and congenital hypothyroidism.
An antimuscarinic eye drop that dilates the pupil and paralyzes accommodation (cycloplegia), used for eye exams.
Placement of a stent graft through the femoral arteries to exclude an aortic aneurysm without open surgery.
Use of a thin scope passed through the urethra and bladder into the ureter to see and treat stones.
Surgical removal of a kidney, done for renal cell carcinoma or donation.
Estrogen mixtures from pregnant mare urine, used as menopausal hormone therapy.
Fracture of the radial shaft with dislocation of the distal radioulnar joint.
Surgical placement of a donor kidney, typically into the iliac fossa, to treat end-stage renal disease.
Lung and airway damage from burning smoke, including thermal injury, soot and carbon monoxide or cyanide poisoning. Hoarseness, singed nasal hair and soot in sputum suggest airway risk.
Endoscopic examination of the esophagus.
Inflation of a balloon in the esophagus or stomach to compress bleeding varices, as with a Sengstaken-Blakemore tube.
Combined imaging fusing metabolic images from positron emission tomography with anatomy from CT, used for cancer staging.
Fluid in the pleural space from cancer spread, often lung or breast. Typically exudative and bloody, with positive cytology.
An instrument for viewing the larynx, used for endotracheal intubation.
Knock-knees, in which the knees angle inward so the ankles are far apart.
A balanced isotonic IV fluid with sodium, potassium, calcium, chloride and lactate.
The knuckle joint between a metacarpal bone and the first finger bone. Commonly involved in rheumatoid arthritis.
Inflammation of the trachea, often bacterial (Staphylococcus aureus) in children, causing stridor and fever.
Passage of sperm through the cumulus and zona pellucida to reach the oocyte. The acrosomal reaction releases enzymes that enable this.
Fibrous joints between skull bones. Premature closure causes craniosynostosis.
A percentile chart comparing a child's height, weight and head circumference to a reference population.
Behavioral and cognitive symptoms caused by brain dysfunction.
Persistent difficulty understanding or producing language, such as aphasia in acquired lesions.
A flexible ring inserted in the vagina releasing estrogen and progestin as contraception for three weeks.
Psoriasis presenting as many small teardrop-shaped scaly plaques, often after streptococcal pharyngitis in young people.
A rare skin condition with tiny, flesh-colored shiny papules, often on genitals, forearms and abdomen.
The ion of fluorine. Strengthens tooth enamel by forming fluorapatite; excess causes fluorosis.
Eruption of primary teeth beginning around 6 months of age.
Asthma caused by workplace exposure to sensitizers, such as isocyanates, flour and latex. Improves away from work.
Perineural fibrosis of the plantar digital nerve between the third and fourth metatarsal heads, causing forefoot burning pain, relieved by removing shoes.
A device that bypasses damaged hair cells by electrically stimulating the auditory nerve, used in profound sensorineural hearing loss.
Softening and thinning of the cervix before labor. Induced with prostaglandins (misoprostol, dinoprostone) or mechanical methods.
Drug analogues of prostaglandins, such as misoprostol, carboprost and alprostadil, used for ulcer protection, labor induction and postpartum hemorrhage.
Abnormal communication between rectum and vagina, causing passage of stool or gas through the vagina. Seen after childbirth injury and in Crohn disease.
A stitch placed around the cervix to prevent premature opening in cervical insufficiency.
Separation of the pubic symphysis, often in pregnancy or childbirth, causing pelvic pain and difficulty walking.
Laboratory assessment of semen for count, motility and morphology, used to evaluate male infertility.
An adrenal androgen precursor made by the zona reticularis. Elevated in adrenal androgen excess, as in congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
Deep, dull, poorly localized pain from internal organs, often referred to somatic areas.
Inflammation of the inner ear labyrinth, causing vertigo with hearing loss and tinnitus, usually viral.
Inflammation of the vestibular nerve, usually viral, causing acute vertigo without hearing loss.
The most common paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia, from a reentry circuit in the AV node with fast and slow pathways. Treated with vagal maneuvers or adenosine.
Surgical removal of the pericardium, treating constrictive pericarditis.
Difficulty identifying and describing one's own emotions.
Eye strain with fatigue, headache and blurred vision after prolonged visual effort.
Rapid, simultaneous eye movements that shift gaze from one point to another. Controlled by the frontal eye fields and paramedian pontine reticular formation.
Protrusion of abdominal contents through a weakness in the abdominal wall, such as inguinal, umbilical or incisional hernia.
Chronic limb pain disproportionate to an injury, with autonomic changes, swelling and altered skin color and temperature.
Minimally invasive chest surgery done through small incisions with a camera.
A protozoan acquired from contaminated water that causes watery diarrhea, severe in AIDS. Oocysts are acid-fast.
Microscopic colitis causing chronic watery diarrhea with a thickened subepithelial collagen band on biopsy and normal-appearing colonoscopy.
Softening of the cartilage under the kneecap causing anterior knee pain, common in young active people.
The outermost layer of the cornea, a non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, which regenerates quickly after abrasions.
Underdevelopment of the left ventricle, aortic and mitral valves and aorta. Circulation depends on a patent ductus arteriosus; presents with cyanosis and shock in the first days.
Hernia through the anterior abdominal wall, including umbilical, epigastric and incisional hernias.
Tissue sampling using imaging such as ultrasound or CT to direct the needle.
Simultaneous intrauterine and ectopic pregnancy, uncommon except after fertility treatment.
Removal of kidney stones through a small incision in the back, used for large stones.
Displacement of the kneecap out of the trochlear groove, usually laterally.
A collection of pus beneath the diaphragm, usually after abdominal surgery or perforation. Causes fever and shoulder pain.
Aortoiliac occlusive disease with buttock claudication, absent femoral pulses and impotence in men.
The largest known protein, spanning from Z disc to M line in sarcomeres, providing elasticity and passive tension to muscle.
Abnormal opening between the inner ear and middle ear causing perilymph leak, vertigo and hearing loss. Follows trauma or pressure change.
Reopening of a surgical wound along the incision, typically 5 to 8 days after surgery. Risk factors include infection and obesity.
Compression of the ulnar nerve at the elbow, causing numbness of the ring and little fingers and weakness of grip.
Congenital cystic dilation of the collecting ducts in renal papillae, associated with kidney stones and hematuria. Gives a paintbrush appearance on urography.
Formation of stones in the urinary tract. Calcium oxalate stones are most common and present with colicky flank pain and hematuria.
Adverse events during surgery, such as bleeding and organ injury.
Migraine preceded by transient focal neurologic symptoms, usually visual (scintillating scotoma), lasting 5 to 60 minutes before headache.
The maximum speed of exhalation measured with a peak flow meter, used to monitor asthma.
A 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor reducing dihydrotestosterone, used for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
Drugs that halt cell proliferation without directly killing cells.
Cutting a circular hole in the skull, practiced since antiquity or used to drain intracranial blood.
A Guillain-Barre variant with ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and areflexia, linked to anti-GQ1b antibodies.
Inherited deficiency in melanin synthesis, usually tyrosinase, causing pale skin and hair, visual impairment and nystagmus, and skin cancer risk.
X-linked reduced pigmentation limited to the eyes, causing nystagmus and reduced visual acuity.
X-ray vessel imaging in which a pre-contrast image is subtracted from later images to show only contrast-filled vessels.
Bleeding into the biliary tract, causing jaundice, biliary colic and GI bleeding after liver trauma or procedures.
A fluid-filled sac in the pancreas, including pseudocysts and neoplastic cysts such as mucinous cystic neoplasm.
Enlargement and flattening of the femoral head, seen after Legg-Calve-Perthes disease.
Weakness with increased tone and hyperreflexia in the legs from corticospinal lesions, as in HTLV-1 associated myelopathy.
Grip force between thumb and finger, a measure of hand function.
Surgical removal of an entire lung.
The coronavirus causing severe acute respiratory syndrome in 2002 to 2003, using ACE2 receptor.
Using laser to clot and seal tissue, as in retinal treatment.
A yeast that often resists fluconazole. Causes bloodstream and urinary infections.
Blocking blood supply to the uterus with particles via catheter, treating fibroids and postpartum hemorrhage.
Lung infection with tissue death and cavity formation, as with Staphylococcus aureus or Klebsiella.
A complement protein of the classical pathway, cleaved to C4a and C4b. Deficiency is linked to lupus.
A neutrophil serine protease that degrades elastin. Alpha-1 antitrypsin normally inhibits it; excess causes emphysema.
Autoimmune disease causing optic neuritis and longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis, with aquaporin-4 antibodies.
Vaccines delivering mRNA in lipid nanoparticles encoding an antigen, as used for COVID-19.
The box jellyfish, with very potent venom that causes severe pain and cardiac arrest.
A lymphoproliferative disorder with enlarged lymph nodes, hyaline-vascular or plasma-cell histology. Linked to HHV-8 and IL-6.
An antifoaming agent for gas, breaking up gas bubbles in the gut.
Gastroenteritis from Campylobacter jejuni, usually from undercooked poultry. A cause of Guillain-Barre syndrome and reactive arthritis.
Bites from ticks, which transmit Lyme disease, ehrlichiosis, Rocky Mountain spotted fever and others.
A protozoan spread by tsetse flies causing acute East African sleeping sickness with rapid course.
A protozoan spread by tsetse flies causing chronic West African sleeping sickness with Winterbottom sign.
Bacterial resistance to chloramphenicol, typically by acetyltransferase enzyme.
Embryonic process converting the bilaminar disc into three germ layers: ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.
A groove on the epiblast in week 3 through which cells move to form mesoderm and endoderm, marking the body axis.
Antipsychotic drug class including chlorpromazine and thioridazine that block dopamine D2 receptors. Cause extrapyramidal effects.
An H2 blocker that reduces gastric acid secretion.
An H2 receptor blocker that reduces gastric acid, used for reflux and ulcers.
A proton pump inhibitor that blocks the gastric H+/K+ ATPase, used for reflux and ulcers.
